novel_features.name: Fleet attention rollup
novel_features.description: One screen merges admin attention + dirty repos + DRaaS-in-progress + open issues, ranked per-company, and persists each call so tomorrow can drift against today.
novel_features.rationale: Composes four real admin endpoints with snapshot persistence — no single API call returns this view, and the web UI requires four-tab clicking.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent or human asks 'what needs my attention right now?' across the whole fleet — it answers in one call instead of four.

novel_features.name: Stale-backup offline query
novel_features.description: Slice the synced /reports/stale-backup-sets/ snapshot by reseller, company, age window, and backup engine — entirely offline once synced. Use --refresh to repull the CSV.
novel_features.rationale: The API ships stale-backup-sets only as a CSV download; the local SQLite snapshot makes it composable with --reseller, --engine, --days filters.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this on Friday's 'who needs a follow-up?' sweep without burning an API call per slice.

novel_features.name: Per-company snapshot
novel_features.description: Single command pulls a company's metadata + addresses + contracts + all backups across three engines + open issues + agent sessions into one human or --json view.
novel_features.rationale: Composes ~7 endpoints plus the cross-engine backup_facts view; the web UI needs five tabs to assemble the same picture.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when a customer asks 'is my backup OK?' — one call, every relevant fact, ready to paste into a ticket.

novel_features.name: Terminal-speed issue triage
novel_features.description: List open issues with filters, then batch ignore / archive / reactivate / comment in one invocation with --dry-run and typed exit codes.
novel_features.rationale: Web UI requires 5+ clicks per issue; this turns a Monday-morning triage into a single piped command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for batch issue actions when the queue is bursty — pipe-friendly, scriptable, idempotent.

novel_features.name: Snapshot drift
novel_features.description: Diff two snapshots the CLI itself collected (attention, stale, dirty-repos) — show what got worse and what recovered between two timestamps.
novel_features.rationale: The web UI has no history surface; only a CLI that captures snapshots over time can answer 'what changed since yesterday?'
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this every morning to surface fleet trend instead of treating every Monday like a fresh slate.

novel_features.name: Cross-engine backup facts
novel_features.description: Query a unified view (engine + id + company_id + last_successful_at + last_status + size_bytes) over all three backup engines synced into the local store.
novel_features.rationale: Three engines (classic / restic / DR) coexist server-side with no unified surface; this view exists only in our local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when you don't care which engine — you just need 'who hasn't backed up successfully since X?' across the whole fleet.

novel_features.name: Cross-table FTS find
novel_features.description: SQLite FTS5 across companies (name, billing notes), issues (title and comments), and backups (descriptive name, last error) — one query hits the whole fleet.
novel_features.rationale: The API has no cross-resource search; the web UI search is per-page. FTS over the synced store is the only path.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when you remember a phrase but not which entity owned it — one call replaces hunting through three list pages.

novel_features.name: Restore-queue oversight
novel_features.description: List per-company restore queues across companies the local store knows about; --watch repolls and prints diffs.
novel_features.rationale: Composes /companies/{id}/restore-queues/ across the fleet — DRaaS in flight needs eyes-on and the web UI is per-company only.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this during an active DR event to keep one terminal pinned on every queue's progress.

novel_features.name: Clear company or partner (until time)
novel_features.description: Resolve one or more names as companies (then resellers) and batch-ignore their active issues until a human-readable time. Defaults to --dry-run for production safety.
novel_features.rationale: Replaces the support team's daily clear-company Python workflow that today is a multi-step shell incantation; the CLI computes ignored_seconds from 6am-tomorrow-style strings and calls /issues/{id}/ignore/ in one shot.
novel_features.example: servosity-pp-cli clear "ACME Corp, BDH Technology" --until "6am tomorrow" --dry-run
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when a partner is doing planned maintenance and you want their alert noise paused until morning — one command instead of dozens of UI clicks.

novel_features.name: Stale-issue cleanup (per support engineer)
novel_features.description: Pull your FMDB companies, fetch active issues, classify known-safe-to-archive patterns from a shipped rule table, auto-archive the safe ones, ignore non-dashboard noise, and print unknowns for review. Defaults to --dry-run.
novel_features.rationale: Replaces the support team's daily morning stale-issue-cleanup Python workflow. The classification rule table ships with the CLI; nothing is LLM-generated.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this every weekday before standup to clear the obvious stale noise off your dashboard so triage focuses on what's actually new.

narrative.headline: Every Servosity endpoint as a typed command, plus a local fleet mirror, snapshot history, and cross-engine rollups the web UI doesn't have.
narrative.value_prop: Every Servosity REST endpoint becomes a typed Cobra command (Resellers, Companies, three backup engines, Issues, Reports, Admin) with `--json`, `--select`, `--csv`, `--dry-run`, and typed exit codes. A local SQLite mirror makes the fleet queryable offline. The attention command answers 'what needs my attention?' across all admin rollups in one call. The drift command tells you what got worse since yesterday. The backup-facts view unifies classic, restic, and DR engines into one view nothing else exposes.
narrative.auth_narrative: Auth is a Servosity API token. Set SERVOSITY_API_TOKEN in your environment (or store it in macOS Keychain as a generic password named SERVOSITY_API_TOKEN and export it from your shell rc) and the CLI sends Authorization: Token <key> on every call — Servosity uses Django REST framework's Token scheme, not Bearer. **The Servosity API is single-tenant production: every mutating command (clear, triage, stale-issues, agent-restart subcommands) defaults to --dry-run; you must drop --dry-run AND pass --confirm to actually call the live API.**

quickstart.comment: Verify the token reaches /resellers/?page_size=1 successfully before doing anything else.
Get the morning fleet rollup: admin attention + dirty repos + DRaaS-in-flight + open issues, ranked per-company.
Pull the /reports/stale-backup-sets/ CSV (use --timeout 180s on big fleets) and slice for >7-day stale sets.
List the first 5 resellers to confirm reads end-to-end. Replace with `sync --resources resellers,companies,issues` once you're ready to populate the local store for offline search and drift.
Pull every relevant fact about a single company across all three engines into one screen.

troubleshoots.fix: Confirm SERVOSITY_API_TOKEN is set and the header format is `Token <key>` (not `Bearer`). Run `servosity-pp-cli doctor` for a clean reachability test.
Your token is scoped below the resource you're hitting (e.g. trying admin endpoints with a reseller-only token). Get a token with the right scope from your Servosity admin.
Run `servosity-pp-cli sync` first — these read from the local SQLite mirror, not live API calls.

troubleshoots.symptom: triage / clear / stale-issues refuse to act
troubleshoots.fix: PLAN mode is the default for production safety. Re-run with `--confirm` to actually call the mutation endpoints (and keep the global `--dry-run` flag off; it overrides --confirm).

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for servosity-pp-cli whenever you need to see the Servosity fleet from the terminal: the morning attention sweep, the Friday stale-backup hunt, ad-hoc 'is ACME OK?' checks, batch issue triage, or DRaaS-in-flight oversight. The local SQLite store and snapshot history make it the right tool for any 'what changed since X?' question — those are unanswerable through the web UI.
